title: Velocity-scaled Opportunity Allocator (VSOA) - blend of RICE and throughput sensitivity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Introduce the Velocity-scaled Opportunity Allocator (VSOA), a prioritization rubric that augments classic RICE inputs (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) with two operational multipliers: throughput sensitivity (how feature changes affect token/throughput efficiency) and latency-friction (how user surface latency shifts change adoption). VSOA is intended for roadmap tradeoffs where per-token cost and SLOs materially influence ROI.

Summary of the approach: VSOA computes a base RICE score, then applies two scaling factors: Velocity Multiplier (VM) and Latency Friction Multiplier (LFM). FinalScore = RICE_base * VM * LFM. VM < 1 penalizes initiatives that reduce throughput efficiency (e.g., adding stateful per-request overhead), VM > 1 rewards initiatives that unlock batching/caching opportunities. LFM < 1 penalizes features that increase perceived latency or SLO risk for high-Traffic routes, LFM > 1 rewards features that reduce tail latency or improve degradation behavior.

Why this is different: Existing prioritization artifacts at Redwood focus heavily on static value metrics or cost-weighted RICE. VSOA explicitly models operational economics (tokens/sec and latency tails) so Platform and Product can align on features that change unit economics. It is particularly useful for: runtime optimizations, SDK changes that alter request patterns, routing policies, and caching features in Redwood Optimize.

Scoring details: 
- Inputs: Reach (R), Impact (I: 0.25/0.5/1/2), Confidence (C 0-100%), Effort (E: points converted to months). RICE_base = (R * I * C) / E.
- Velocity Multiplier (VM): estimated percentage change in tokens/sec or cost per token, normalized to [0.6, 1.4] where 1.0 = neutral. Example: Adding aggressive KV caching = VM 1.25; introducing per-request signature verification = VM 0.8.
- Latency Friction Multiplier (LFM): derived from modeled change to 95th/99th latency for top routes, normalized to [0.7, 1.2]. Example: feature that reduces 99th latency by 20% -> LFM 1.15.
- FinalScore example: RICE_base 120 * VM 1.10 * LFM 0.95 = 125.4.

Trade-offs and calibration: The calibration bands for VM and LFM were derived from historical telemetry (token/sec variance and customer churn signals) and a small set of experiments (see linked dashboard). We maintain conservative caps to avoid extreme swings. Product and Platform owners must document assumptions for both multipliers and attach a short telemetry plan for validation.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Guidance for PMs: Use VSOA for initiatives where estimated per-token cost change > 5% or where SLO changes > 5th percentile of route latency. For purely UX or policy work with negligible throughput/latency impact, fall back to standard RICE.

Governance: Each VSOA-scored initiative must have: 1) telemetry hypothesis (dashboard + metrics), 2) a rollback/fallback plan if latency or cost regressions exceed guardrails, 3) a post-launch evaluation in the next cycle.
